prior_attempt.rejection: The first correction separated state borders from arrows, but treated stateArrowColor as unconditionally more specific than ArrowColor. Java normalizes both spellings to the same arrowColor style property, so their declarations override in source order.

second_rejection.rejection: The renderer's unified reverse alias lookup was correct for distinct parsed keys, but parse::collapse_reassigned_skinparams had already collapsed repeated raw spellings independently. It retained each raw key's first position, so a later repeated stateArrowColor could still sort before an intervening ArrowColor even though Java canonicalizes all family-arrow aliases before updating one map entry.

third_rejection.rejection: The parser compared ordinary declarations by the right cleaned identity but retained the first raw spelling, which downstream renderers cannot necessarily recognize after separator and family-arrow normalization. It also treated the appended synthetic theme tail as temporally later than every user declaration. PlantUML executes a theme synchronously where its directive occurs, so user skinparams after !theme must override theme values.

failed_broad_validation.implementation: Canonicalize every non-internal parsed skinparam before reassignment collapse.
failed_broad_validation.evidence: The full no-oracle census fell from 11049/11251 to 11033/11251, entirely in preprocessing (264/307 to 248/307), while state remained 882/901. Theme-expanded diagrams exposed the missing provenance boundary.
failed_broad_validation.finding: RustUML appends `__theme` followed by flattened entries from every theme family sub-block. Keys such as classArrowColor, stateArrowColor, and usecaseArrowColor in that synthetic tail represent distinct style scopes selected later by each renderer; they are not one sequence of user SkinParam.setParam calls. Applying Java ordinary-key canonicalization to the synthetic tail merged those scopes and destroyed the family-specific compatibility model.

invariant: Java resolves state-image borders and state-diagram arrows from sibling style signatures. FromSkinparamToStyle maps stateBorderColor to root.element.stateDiagram.state LineColor. Before either its parameter map or style conversion sees an ordinary declaration, SkinParam.cleanForKeySlow lowercases and trims the key, removes underscores and dots, rewrites sequenceParticipant/sequenceActor aliases, rewrites every activity/class/component/object/sequence/state/usecase Arrow prefix to the shared arrow prefix, and rewrites a terminal align to alignment. SkinParam.setParam stores that cleaned key, so the effective metadata crossing into Rust renderers must expose the cleaned identity rather than an arbitrary first raw spelling. TContext.executeOneLineNotSafe dispatches a THEME line immediately to executeTheme, which reads the theme and calls executeLines before processing the next user line. Theme styles therefore occupy the directive's temporal position: user declarations before a theme can be superseded by it, and user declarations after it supersede matching theme properties. RustUML may continue relocating flattened theme output to preserve source-line numbers, but parser metadata must reconstruct this source order. Flattened theme family sub-blocks remain distinct scoped compatibility records and must not be merged by ordinary SkinParam family-arrow aliases. GraphvizImageBuilder and SvekEdge independently merge the selected arrow signature and derive the shaft and arrowhead Rainbow from it. The arrow signature may inherit the root or theme line color, but never the state sibling's explicit LineColor. A per-link color remains the final arrow-only override.
causal_divergence: Commit 2ddfe4b1 computes the right ordinary cleanForKey identity only as a hidden comparison key. It leaves the retained SkinParam.key as the first raw spelling, so a final value stored under StAtE_ArRoW.CoLoR is invisible to StateSkin's stateArrowColor/ArrowColor lookup and inherited arrows fall back to #181818. Separately, preprocess::try_theme appends both the __theme marker and flattened body after the entire diagram. A user state-arrow declaration located after !theme is therefore represented before the theme tail, and the renderer's reverse scan selects the theme value. Java executes the theme body at the directive and then applies that later user declaration. The two review-3 heldouts isolate these as inherited-arrow color differences while per-link overrides remain correct.
planned_change: Keep theme expansion physically relocated for source-line stability, but emit an in-place ordered theme marker and delimit each appended flattened theme body with internal metadata. In collapse_reassigned_skinparams, reconstruct one logical event stream by splicing each synthetic body at its matching marker. Preserve raw family-scoped identities inside those bodies; process user-authored ordinary declarations with cleanForKey identity regardless of whether they occur before or after a theme. Retain only the last ordinary declaration for each cleaned identity at its effective source position and store the cleaned key itself so every renderer can consume it. Preserve unrelated double-underscore metadata in order. Add parser tests for separator aliases, alternating family-arrow aliases, theme-before-user and user-before-theme precedence, repeated themes, and distinct class/state/usecase theme scopes. Keep stateBorderColor isolation and per-transition final override unchanged. Preserve every existing and review-3 heldout. Do not special-case fixture labels, colors, branch counts, or SVG output.
